11th Degree Chords · Level 1.heading: Hear the full chord. Choose its type.
11th Degree Chords · Level 1.intro: You will hear a chord with an eleventh or a raised eleventh added. Choose the chord name that matches its sound.

steps.title: Listen to the whole chord
steps.description: Press Play and listen to the notes together. Focus on the sound of the whole chord rather than trying to name every note. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the chord type
steps.description: Choose one of the six chord names shown. Pay attention to the full name: a raised eleventh, a lowered ninth or a lowered fifth changes the sound.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

11th Degree Chords · Level 1.about: These chords build on seventh and ninth chords by adding an eleventh or a raised eleventh. For example, F minor eleventh uses F, A♭, C, E♭, G and B♭. In the answer names, ♯11 means a raised eleventh, ♭9 means a lowered ninth, and ♭5 means a lowered fifth. Raising or lowering a note means moving one keyboard step, counting both white and black keys. This lesson uses chords built on F. The chords start with their root, the note they are named after, at the bottom. Choose only the chord type; there is no separate inversion answer.
11th Degree Chords · Level 1.layoutCaption: F minor eleventh, with all six chord notes played together.
11th Degree Chords · Level 1.exampleExplanation: This visual example is F minor eleventh. Choose Minor 11th. During the quiz, listen to the whole chord and select the matching name, even when the notes are arranged differently.
